## Overview

LRP65 is the Bayesian "interpretable estimand" follow-up to the LightGBM discovery
layer (LRP01). It answers the **static, between-child** question raised by the
descriptive work and the meeting: *do children who start (at wave 1) with more
letter-sound knowledge / language / blending go on to gain more in word reading?*

The candidate predictors form a correlated general-ability cluster (vocabulary–block
design $\rho \approx 0.63$; vocabulary–letter-sounds $\approx 0.4$–$0.5$), so a naive
"throw them all in" regression is multicollinear and "independent predictor" is
ambiguous. The DAG below fixes the estimand and the adjustment set **before** fitting.

## Estimand and design

_Between-child association — match the design to the estimand._ The estimand is the **mutually-adjusted between-child association** of each wave-1
baseline skill with subsequent word-reading gain, holding the other measured baselines
and $W_{\text{pre}}$ constant, *across children*.

The model uses one row per child. Predictors are measured at t1, and the outcome is word reading at the last wave, adjusted for word reading at t1. It therefore estimates between-child associations and has no child random intercept.

A repeated-period model with a random intercept would generally combine between-child and within-child associations unless it separated them explicitly. The intercept would not remove confounding by unmeasured general ability. Both designs remain associational; the choice here follows the one-row-per-child question.

These are **associations, not causal effects** (n ≈ 51). The corresponding randomised-arm
result is the available-case modified ITT estimate in `lrp-rli-itt-010` (which supersedes
LRP52); the randomised gain-side coefficient lives in `lrp-rli-gf-001`.

![Causal DAG. Latent general ability `g` (dashed, not fitted) drives the correlated T1 baselines; hearing status, speech production and phonological memory sit upstream of the skill cluster (revised DAG, #247); the dashed edges from non-verbal MA, behaviour, SES and the three upstream traits to gain are the associations the model is built to test.](dag.svg){#fig-dag .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Adjustment set and predictors

- **Predictors of interest (standardised T1, per-SD):** letter sounds (`yarclet`), an
  equal-weight **language composite** (ROWPVT + EOWPVT + CELF), blending, age.
- **Baseline conditioning:** $W_{\text{pre}}$ (T1 word reading) via $\gamma_{\text{own}}$.
- **Tested covariates:** non-verbal MA (block design) and behaviour, plus — under the
  revised 2026-07-10 DAG (#247) — the three upstream traits it places above the
  baseline-skill cluster: hearing status (`hs`, a 0/1 flag derived from the hearing
  composite), speech production (`deapp_c`) and phonological memory (`erbto`), each
  entered by the missing-indicator method so no child is dropped for a missing trait.
  All are entered to *demonstrate* whether they carry independent signal. SES is
  adjudicated in a separate complete-case sensitivity fit (it has notable missingness).
- **Units.** Every predictor is standardised on the fitted children, so each slope is
  per SD. Hearing status is a binary flag (29 clear / 25 impaired at t1), so its "+1 SD"
  rows are roughly half the clear-versus-impaired contrast; the `_missing` indicators are
  nuisance subgroup offsets and are kept out of the association tables. Randomised arm is
  **not** in the model: by randomisation it is orthogonal to the t1 predictors in
  expectation (the realised imbalance is ≤ 0.22 SD on any predictor), so it is a
  precision choice rather than a confounding one; the t1→t4 window contains both arms'
  intervention periods at different times.

Each predictor's **adjusted** (mutual) coefficient is reported alongside its **bivariate**
(baseline-only-adjusted) association, so the shared-variance shift is visible. The
items-scale contrasts are evaluated at one operating point — a child at the sample-mean
t1 word-reading logit with every other standardised predictor at zero — for two such
children who differ by one SD on one predictor; the prior pushforward uses the same
functional.
